title: China's Hesai launches spatial camera to boost AI-powered robotics adoption
key_facts: Hesai Group launched Kosmo on 14 Oct 2026, a 3D world data engine combining the Kosmo One spatial camera with the Kosmo World cloud platform.
The system turns real spaces into 3D digital scenes for robot training, world-model development and content creation.
Hesai also announced partnerships with embodied-AI companies Galbot and Dexmal.
Hesai says a single operator can scan a typical 100-square-metre room in about 15 minutes.
At a Dairy Queen store, Hesai says building a training scene took 15 minutes instead of about 300 hours of manual modelling, and a Sharpa robot's task success reached 99%.
Hesai co-founder and CTO Shaoqing Xiang said physical AI needs real-world data that is accurate, affordable and available at scale.
quote_evidence: Hesai Group launched Kosmo on October 14, 2026, a 3D world data engine that combines its Kosmo One spatial camera with the Kosmo World cloud platform, converting physical environments into high-fidelity 3D digital spaces used for robot training, world model development, and immersive content creation.
The Kosmo One is an 8K ultra-high-definition AI spatial camera combining high-resolution lidar, a one-inch imaging sensor, and a high-precision inertial measurement unit
why_it_matters_hint: A lidar maker is targeting the shortage of real-world 3D training data for robots.
